title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 408 (Constitution of National Company Law Tribunal)

content.overview: The Central Government constitutes the National Company Law Tribunal to exercise and discharge the powers and functions conferred on the Tribunal by the Act.
content.glance: The Central Government constitutes the National Company Law Tribunal to exercise and discharge the powers and functions conferred on the Tribunal by the Act.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 408 (Constitution of National Company Law Tribunal). The Central Government constitutes the National Company Law Tribunal to exercise and discharge the powers and functions conferred on the Tribunal by the Act. Apply only the conditions, approvals, filings and penalties stated in the section. A rule made under the Act cannot contradict the section. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: The Central Government constitutes the National Company Law Tribunal to exercise and discharge the powers and functions conferred on the Tribunal by the Act.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: The Tribunal is the company-law forum and the adjudicating authority under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. Benches sit at the places notified.
